claims.text: The alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The WTaTiVZr alloy is produced by powder metallurgy.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has a BCC-dominant structure.
The BCC matrix of WTaTiVZr may contain short-range chemical order.
Chemical complexity in WTaTiVZr produces regions of short-range chemical order.
Short-range chemical order interacts with dislocations and stabilizes dislocation glide.
Short-range chemical order promotes a more homogeneous distribution of dislocation motion and mitigates localized slip banding.
Interactions between short-range order and dislocations promote forest hardening.
More homogeneous dislocation motion delays microcrack nucleation.
Delayed crack nucleation enhances plastic strain and fracture toughness in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten has more heterogeneous dislocation motion and is more prone to localized strain accumulation than WTaTiVZr under the proposed conditions.
Pure tungsten exhibits earlier crack nucleation and less plastic deformation than WTaTiVZr under otherwise similar high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure and greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten at 800–1200 °C under simulated plasma-facing conditions.
In-situ imaging will show more homogeneous dislocation activity and delayed crack formation in WTaTiVZr relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed advantage depends on elevated temperature providing sufficient thermal activation for dislocation mobility.
The proposed advantage may not occur at room temperature.
The influence of local chemical order on dislocation kinetics under irradiation remains unestablished.
Matching grain size and processing history between WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten provides a controlled comparison.
A lack of delayed crack initiation together with similarly heterogeneous dislocation motion and fracture behavior would falsify the proposed mechanism.
